findings.claim: The new `prewarmModules: false` property is added inside an object written with a type assertion (`<Environment>{...}`), which does not apply excess-property checking. If `prewarmModules` is not actually declared on the `Environment` interface (or is spelled differently there, e.g. `prewarm`/`preloadModules`), TypeScript will silently accept it and the flag will be a no-op at runtime.
findings.rationale: Type assertions on object literals only require comparability, so extra/misspelled keys compile cleanly. Worth verifying the property exists on the `Environment` type (and is read by the runner) — medium confidence, since I cannot see the type definition in this hunk.

findings.claim: Disabling prewarming for the `node` environment is a behavior change for the default environment: every project that does not explicitly set `environment` now loses module prewarming, which could regress startup/run time or change module-instantiation ordering observed by existing tests.
findings.rationale: `node` is Vitest's default environment, so this opt-out applies to the vast majority of users rather than a niche env. If the intent was only to skip prewarming in the VM path (`setupVM`), a per-environment static flag applies to both `setup()` and `setupVM()`. Low-to-medium confidence that this is unintended, but it is a broad, silent behavior change worth confirming.

findings.claim: Only the node environment declares `prewarmModules`; other built-in environments (jsdom, happy-dom, edge-runtime) presumably still rely on an implicit default. If the consuming code reads `env.prewarmModules` without a defined default (e.g. `if (env.prewarmModules)` vs `!== false`), the undefined value in the other environments may be coerced to the opposite of the intended default.
findings.rationale: Introducing an optional tri-state (true/false/undefined) flag is easy to mishandle at the call site; the default semantics for the environments that omit it should be explicit. Low confidence without seeing the consumer, but a plausible source of inconsistency.
